description: Search the adopted budget's Terms and Conditions (the conditions the Council attaches to agencies' appropriations, with the reports they require), FY2018 and FY2021–FY2027, from the checked tables BetaNYC reads from the PDFs. Each item gives its number in the book, pages, agency, units of appropriation, budget lines, report deadlines and the condition's text as printed, with its status label, flags, review decision where decided, and three links. Filter by fiscal_year, agency (name or code, substring), unit (a unit of appropriation as printed, e.g. '001', or the start of a budget line), text (substring of the condition or its heading). The same filters as the explorer's Terms view. Needs the optional PDF tables download. Text filters match case- and accent-insensitive substrings, except that a term of 3 or fewer letters and digits matches whole words ('AI' does not match 'Jamaica'); whole_word overrides that for the call, and the answer says when it applied. Identifier filters (project_id, resolution_number) always match substrings.

agency.description: Agency name or code (substring), e.g. 'Correction' or '072'

limit.description: Max items shown, 1–100 (default 20). Counts always cover every match.

text.description: Words in the condition's text or heading (substring)

unit.description: Unit of appropriation as printed ('001', 'All'), or the start of a budget line ('HD-0009')

whole_word.description: How this call's text filters match. Omit it for the default: a term of 3 or fewer letters and digits (after trimming) matches whole words, a longer term matches anywhere, as a substring. true: every name and prose filter matches whole words only, the term not inside a longer word ('AI' finds 'AI Training Program', '(AI)', 'AI-powered', 'BetaNYC's AI', but not 'Jamaica' or 'AIDS'). false: every name and prose filter matches substrings. Pass false to find a short term inside words (e.g. 'AI' inside 'AIDS'); pass true to keep a longer word from matching longer ones ('Fellow' but not 'Fellowship'). Case, accents and punctuation folding are the same either way, and % and _ stay literal. It applies to name and prose filters only: identifier filters (project_id, resolution_number) always match substrings, so an ID fragment such as 'CC1' or '101' finds the IDs that contain it, and exact filters (EIN, IDs, budget line, codes, city, zip) are not affected. The answer says which filters matched as whole words.

name: search_terms_conditions
